overview: State Bank of India (SBI) is India's largest commercial bank by assets and deposits, with roots going back over 200 years and majority ownership (~57%) by the Government of India. The bank operates a vast domestic franchise of over 23,000 branches and 64,000+ ATMs serving more than 53 crore (530 million) customers, alongside an International Banking Group with ~245 foreign offices/branches and a broad network of financial-services subsidiaries (SBI Life, SBI Cards, SBI Funds Management, SBI General Insurance, SBI Capital Markets). Standalone banking (retail, corporate, agri/rural, SME, treasury and international banking) drives the bulk of consolidated earnings, with listed and unlisted subsidiaries providing an increasingly valuable, separately monetizable fee-income and insurance/asset-management layer on top of the core lending business.

business_model.summary: SBI earns net interest income by taking low-cost retail/CASA and term deposits and deploying them into retail, agricultural, SME, corporate and international loans, supplemented by fee and non-interest income (government business, transaction banking, treasury gains) and dividends/consolidated profits from financial subsidiaries. Reporting here is on a standalone (bank-only) basis in INR millions; the broader 'SBI Group' consolidates SBI Life (insurance), SBI Cards (credit cards), SBI Funds Management (asset management, now separately listed), SBI General Insurance and SBI Capital Markets, each with its own minority shareholders and, increasingly, public listings.

revenue_streams.name: Subsidiaries (SBI Life, SBI Cards, SBI Funds Mgmt, SBI General Insurance) - consolidated contribution

business_model.customer_type: Mass-market retail/consumer (B2C), SME, agricultural/rural, large corporate (B2B), government/PSU, and international/NRI banking
business_model.geographic_mix: Predominantly domestic India (~85-90% of advances), with International Banking Group operations across ~29 countries via subsidiaries/branches in UK, US, Canada, Mauritius, Indonesia, Nepal, Bhutan and representative/correspondent relationships in 56+ countries

competitive_position.market_position: Clear market leader - largest bank in India by assets, deposits and advances (~30% share of installed ATM network), dominant in government banking (63% share of Central Government turnover) and the largest public-sector bank; roughly one in four Indian banking customers banks with SBI

moat_factors.description: 23,265 domestic branches and 64,245 ATMs give unmatched physical distribution, especially in rural and semi-urban India where private banks have thinner presence
CASA ratio of ~39-40% and India's largest low-cost deposit base provide a structural funding-cost advantage over smaller/private peers
~57% government ownership confers a quasi-sovereign credit halo, lowest-cost wholesale funding (AAA domestic ratings) and systemic-importance status ('too big to fail')
Accredited banker to 26 central ministries/departments and dominant share of government salary, pension and treasury business creates sticky, low-cost liability flows

YONO super-app has 11+ crore registered users and drives ~90% of new digitally-sourced savings accounts, narrowing the digital gap with private banks, though still playing catch-up to HDFC/ICICI/Kotak digital UX
Captive distribution for SBI Life, SBI Cards, SBI General Insurance and SBI Funds Management through the branch network, though each subsidiary also faces standalone competitive pressure

weaknesses: Legacy technology stack and bureaucratic PSU decision-making slow relative to nimble private-sector digital banks
Lower fee income and cross-sell intensity per customer than HDFC Bank/ICICI Bank, weighing on cost-to-income and RoA versus top private peers
Government ownership constrains compensation, talent retention and capital-raising flexibility (FM/RBI/Parliament oversight)
Rising share of unsecured retail lending (personal loans, credit cards via SBI Cards) across the group increases tail risk if consumer credit cycle turns
NIM structurally below top private banks due to deposit mix, PSL/priority-sector obligations and rate-sensitive wholesale book

growth_drivers: Continued double-digit credit growth (management guidance of 13-15% loan growth) led by Retail Personal, Agri and SME (RAM) segments growing faster than corporate
YONO digital platform scale-up - ~4 crore new YONO users added in FY2026, driving low-cost account acquisition and cross-sell of loans/insurance

Subsidiary value unlocking - SBI Funds Management completed its IPO/listing in July 2026 (~Rs 11,692 crore OFS), following SBI Cards and SBI Life as separately listed, market-valued entities, highlighting embedded group value not fully reflected in the standalone bank multiple

₹25,000 crore QIP (largest-ever Indian equity QIP, July 2025) strengthened capital (CET1/CAR comfortably above regulatory minimums at ~15.4-16%), supporting continued balance-sheet growth without near-term dilution risk
Financial inclusion / rural and MSME penetration - SHG loan portfolio past ₹64,000 crore, agri lending past ₹4 trillion, Business Correspondent network of 79,000+ outlets
Government capex and infrastructure cycle, PM Surya Ghar rooftop solar financing (73.84% market share) and continued corporate capex recovery supporting the corporate/SME book
Operating leverage from digital transaction migration - 98.7%+ of transactions now through alternate (non-branch) channels, supporting cost-to-income improvement

business.risk: Asset quality reversal in unsecured/retail and agri/SME books
business.description: Group-wide unsecured retail exposure has risen to ~28-29% of retail loans from ~17% a decade ago; rapid agri (22-25% YoY) and SME (~22% YoY) growth, partly under government credit-guarantee schemes, raises questions about underwriting quality even though headline GNPA/NNPA are at multi-decade lows (GNPA ~1.4%, NNPA ~0.36-0.39%)
HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank, Axis Bank and Kotak continue to out-execute on digital UX, fee income and cross-sell, pressuring SBI's market share in profitable retail/SME segments
Domestic NIM has been range-bound around 3.0-3.5% and sensitive to deposit repricing lag versus loan repricing in a falling/neutral rate environment

financial.description: Despite the FY2025 QIP, sustained 15%+ credit growth will require periodic capital raises, diluting existing shareholders over time
Large government securities portfolio exposes earnings to bond-yield swings, though ECL/Basel transitions are being phased in

regulatory.description: As a majority government-owned entity, SBI is subject to directed lending priorities, government business mandates, and periodic political/policy pressure that can override pure commercial decision-making

RBI's rollout of the Expected Credit Loss (ECL) provisioning framework, revised Basel standardised approach for credit risk, and deposit insurance premium changes could affect provisioning levels, capital ratios and cost structure
Minimum public shareholding and SEBI disclosure norms for now-listed subsidiaries (SBI Cards, SBI Life, SBI Funds Management) add complexity to group capital allocation and stake-sale decisions

macro.description: FY2026 annual report flags an outbreak of conflict in West Asia (Strait of Hormuz disruption, oil near $110/bbl) as a live risk to India's growth, inflation and trade outlook into FY2027, with GDP growth guidance trimmed to ~6.9%
As India's largest lender, SBI's loan growth, NIM and credit costs are tightly linked to RBI rate policy (repo held at 5.25% as of FY2026-end) and the domestic business cycle
Rising global commodity/energy prices and INR volatility can pressure corporate borrower health (especially SME/mid-corporate segments) and import-dependent sectors

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Indian banking sector advances are expected to grow ~13-14% in FY2027 per management/industry commentary, with public-sector bank capital adequacy, NIMs (~3% average) and asset quality at multi-decade highs/lows (strong) as of March 2026; India's GDP grew 7.6% in FY2026 and is projected at ~6.9% in FY2027, still among the fastest-growing major economies, though global growth is projected to slow (IMF: 3.4%->3.1%) amid the West Asia conflict
macro_factors.cyclicality: Moderate-to-high - bank earnings (NIM, credit costs, loan growth) are tied to India's GDP, rate and credit cycles, though SBI's deposit-funded, diversified book is less volatile than monoline lenders
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: High - RBI repo rate moves directly affect NIM, deposit costs and loan repricing; RBI held repo at 5.25% with a neutral stance as of FY2026-end, with rates expected to stay steady near-term

recent_developments.event: Standalone net profit rose 14.3% YoY to Rs 23,038 crore; NII up 14.7% to Rs 49,143 crore; Gross NPA fell to 1.39% (lowest in 20+ years), Net NPA 0.36%; domestic NIM improved 3 bps QoQ to 3.11% though whole-bank NIM dipped 2 bps YoY to 2.94%; some analysts flagged a large exceptional gain inflating reported operating profit versus underlying pre-provision operating profit, which fell YoY

SBI Funds Management (SBI Mutual Fund) completed its IPO/listing (100% offer-for-sale, ~Rs 11,000-12,000 crore), becoming SBI's third listed subsidiary after SBI Cards and SBI Life; management said no further stake dilution in the AMC is planned near-term

SBI completed a record Rs 25,000 crore QIP - the largest ever in Indian capital markets - with bids of ~Rs 1 trillion led by LIC and domestic mutual funds; more than 64% of allotted bids came from foreign investors, strengthening CET1/CAR to ~15-16%

Gross NPA ratio fell 36 bps YoY to ~1.47%, described by management/analysts as the lowest in over two decades; Chairman CS Setty dismissed asset-quality stress concerns despite rapid agri (+25%) and SME (+22%) loan growth, maintaining 14-15% credit-growth guidance for FY2027
FY2026 standalone net profit crossed Rs 80,032 crore (up 12.9% YoY), total business surpassed Rs 109 trillion, ROA reached 1.12% and ROE 18.57%; dividend per share raised to Rs 17.35

FY2026 annual report cites an outbreak of conflict in West Asia disrupting the Strait of Hormuz and global energy/trade flows as a live macro risk clouding the FY2027 outlook, alongside continued RBI reforms (ECL framework, Basel standardised approach revisions)

Stock price hit a series of record highs during 2026 (market cap crossing ~Rs 8.96-9.5 lakh crore at various points), with brokerages (Jefferies, Nomura, CLSA, Motilal Oswal, Axis Securities) broadly maintaining Buy/Outperform ratings and raising target prices (range roughly Rs 1,120-1,337) through the year, though some flagged that re-rating in the P/B multiple has priced in much of the near-term growth

guidance.as_of: Q2 FY2027 Earnings / FY2026 Annual Report (management commentary, Nov 2026 and Chairman's message)

items.notes: Management (Chairman CS Setty) reiterated 14-15% credit-growth guidance despite a quarter-on-quarter NPA uptick attributed to seasonal factors; aligns with bank-sector-wide advances growth guidance of 13-14% in FY2027
Management previously committed to keeping ROA above 1% despite margin pressure from an easing rate cycle; FY2026 actual ROA came in at 1.12%, slightly ahead of this threshold
Management guidance that it does not expect significant stress in SME or unsecured retail portfolios, aiming to keep slippages contained even as those segments grow faster than the overall book

Strengthened via the Rs 25,000 crore QIP (July 2025); CAR stood at 15.40% at FY2026-end and 16.09% as of Sep 2026, comfortably above regulatory minimums, supporting continued double-digit balance-sheet growth without near-term equity dilution

items.metric: India GDP growth (macro backdrop cited by management)
items.notes: FY2026 Annual Report's Directors' Report revised its FY2027 real GDP growth outlook down modestly, citing the West Asia conflict and related energy/trade disruption as a downside risk; inflation expected to rise to ~4.6% in FY2027 but remain within RBI's mandate

guidance.management_commentary: Chairman CS Setty has repeatedly dismissed asset-quality stress concerns from rapid agri and SME growth, framing the current GNPA/NNPA ratios (near multi-decade lows) as reflective of disciplined underwriting rather than under-recognition of risk. Management continues to emphasize the 'Digital First, Customer First, Nation Always' strategy, with YONO adoption, subsidiary value-unlocking (SBI Funds Management listing) and balance-sheet capital strength (post-QIP) cited as key supports for sustaining growth into FY2027, while flagging the West Asia conflict and a protracted global slowdown as watch-items for asset quality and credit demand.

bull_case: Unmatched scale and low-cost CASA/deposit franchise give SBI a structural funding-cost advantage that underpins industry-leading NIM resilience and double-digit loan growth (13-15% guided) even in a competitive market
Asset quality is at multi-decade bests (GNPA ~1.4%, NNPA ~0.36-0.39%, PCR >90%), reducing credit-cost risk and supporting sustained ROA >1.1% and ROE near 18-19%
Capital position was meaningfully strengthened by the record Rs 25,000 crore QIP (2025), removing near-term dilution overhang while funding continued balance-sheet expansion

Hidden value in listed and soon-to-be-listed subsidiaries (SBI Cards, SBI Life, newly-listed SBI Funds Management, SBI General Insurance) that the market may not fully price into the standalone bank's valuation, offering potential re-rating/SOTP upside (brokerage SOTP targets of Rs 1,275-1,337)

Digital transformation (YONO, 11+ crore registered users, 98.7% of transactions via alternate channels) is narrowing the technology/customer-experience gap with private-sector peers while leveraging SBI's unmatched physical distribution
bear_case: Government ownership (~57%) brings governance, compensation and strategic-flexibility constraints, and periodic policy-directed lending that can dilute purely commercial decision-making versus nimbler private banks

Rapid growth in higher-risk segments - unsecured retail (now ~28-29% of retail loans, up from ~17% a decade ago), agri (+22-25% YoY) and SME (+22% YoY), partly via government credit-guarantee schemes - raises the risk of a delayed asset-quality reversal once the credit cycle turns, even though current NPA ratios look pristine

Valuation has already re-rated meaningfully (P/B near multi-year highs, stock hitting repeated record highs through 2026), reducing the margin of safety and making further upside dependent on flawless execution of growth and asset-quality guidance
Persistent competitive pressure from HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank, Axis Bank and Kotak Mahindra Bank in high-margin retail/SME/digital banking could erode SBI's market share and fee-income growth over time

Macro/geopolitical risk flagged directly by management - an active West Asia conflict disrupting energy and trade flows, a slower global growth backdrop (IMF cutting 2026 global growth to 3.1%), and a downward revision to India's FY2027 GDP outlook (6.9%) - could pressure credit demand, margins and asset quality across the loan book simultaneously
